punchline: Rereading, the way most students study, mostly teaches you that the page looks familiar.
thirty_sec: Most students say their main study method is rereading. The authors of Make It Stick say it barely helps. Each pass makes the text feel familiar, and we mistake that for knowing it. What works is harder: closing the book and quizzing yourself. The effort strengthens the memory and shows your gaps. In classroom studies, material covered by quick, low-stakes quizzes was remembered better on later exams than material that was just reviewed.
question: Can you remember a time you were sure you knew something until you had to explain it without your notes?
